comparison: Both evaluate force-probe MD simulations (C10, C134-C137) showing cholesterol stabilization of tetramer interfaces. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and rate-dependent effects. Peer review rates it UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting the results are suggestive but requesting free energy calculations for full support of the stabilization effect.

Both address systematic reconstitution experiments across lipid ratios (C45-C49, C54). OpenEval finds crystallographic evidence fully SUPPORTED. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 praising the multiple lipid compositions as a strength and Reviewer 2 noting the thorough approach.

Both evaluate MD simulations of cholesterol binding (C4, C5, C111-C112, C115, C118). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with sufficient sampling time and validation of structural observations. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewers 2 and 3 confirming the simulations demonstrate well-defined cholesterol localization around AQP0 tetramers.

Both address surface complementarity and mechanical stability (C150-C152, plus C11, C142-C143 in peer review). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes the mechanistic interpretation is somewhat speculative. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting the complementarity analysis as supporting evidence without challenge.

Both evaluate membrane thickness changes with cholesterol (C6, C177-C178, C109-C110) and hydrophobic mismatch clustering mechanism (C192-C193). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable inference about clustering. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the measurements and interpretation as consistent with the data.

Both address Chol3's unusual deep position (C104-C106, C8-C9, C119, C129, C131). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with detailed structural characterization. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewers 2 and 3 explicitly confirming identification of the unusual cholesterol position stabilized by adjacent tetramers.

Both evaluate generalization to lipid raft biology (C7, C14). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the extrapolation is highly speculative without validation in other systems. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 explicitly stating the broader applicability is 'less clear' given the unique nature of lens membranes.

OpenEval R9 addresses MD simulations comparing cholesterol behavior across membrane environments (C9, C120-C131), finding SUPPORTED. Peer R3 addresses the unusual Chol3 position (C8-C9, C104-C106, C119, C129, C131), also SUPPORTED. Both confirm tetramer pairing stabilizes deep cholesterol, with overlapping claims C9, C129, C131.

Both address electron crystallography structure determination (C3, C62, C82). OpenEval R3 provides detailed evaluation of data collection and structural observations (C60-C78), rating SUPPORTED. Peer R1 also rates SUPPORTED, with all reviewers acknowledging the crystallography as 'compelling' and 'thorough.'

OpenEval R4 evaluates improved crystal quality and lipid substitutions (C79-C94), rating SUPPORTED. Peer R9 addresses structural comparisons and lipid positions (C66-C67, C85-C86, C88), also SUPPORTED. Both accept the structural conservation across lipid environments with overlapping claims on sphingomyelin substitution.

Both address cholesterol's role in array formation. OpenEval R13 (C12-C13, C207-C213) rates UNCERTAIN due to extrapolation from dimer to larger arrays without validation. Peer R6 (C7, C13, C193) rates SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the model as reasonable and consistent with data, though acknowledging it is speculative.

Both address lipid-protein interactions and sphingomyelin's role (C153-C158, C155, C69). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, concluding sphingomyelin is not the primary driver of array formation. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting the structural comparisons without challenge.

OpenEval R11 addresses interface composition and contact dynamics from MD simulations (C138-C149), rating SUPPORTED. Peer R7 addresses protein-protein interactions and surface complementarity (C11, C142-C143, C150-C152), also SUPPORTED. Both accept the MD findings on interface characteristics.

OpenEval R2 evaluates the narrow LPR window for pure cholesterol membrane formation (C51-C53), rating SUPPORTED with reasonable inference based on cholesterol's bilayer requirements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval R5 evaluates consistent Chol1 positioning and specific molecular interactions (C95-C103), rating SUPPORTED with reproducibility across conditions supporting a 'preferred' binding site. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific Chol1 claims.

OpenEval R15 evaluates absence of sphingomyelin-cholesterol interactions and exclusion of phase separation as primary driver (C163-C174), rating SUPPORTED based on B-factor analysis and mechanistic reasoning. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these phase separation claims.

OpenEval R16 evaluates SM3 as the extracellular leaflet anchor (C180-C187), rating SUPPORTED based on consistent structural features across all AQP0 structures. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific SM3 anchor claims.

OpenEval R17 evaluates absence of consensus cholesterol binding motifs and α face interaction mode (C194-C202), rating SUPPORTED with mechanistic explanation for interaction specificity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these binding motif claims.
